name: Hydra
comment: TextMate grammar for the Hydra textual syntax (.hydra). Single source of truth for highlighting, derived from docs/specification/syntax.md (#497 lexical/term/type grammar, #710/#6 module grammar, #809 nominal sugar). See #806. A TextMate grammar only TOKENIZES, never rejects; forms reserved for #811 (operator / do-block / destructuring-pattern sugar) that are not yet accepted by the parser are included here and tagged 'forward-looking (#811)' in their own comment keys.

expression.comment: Everything that can appear in term/type position. Lexical patterns (literals, strings, names) come before structural keywords so e.g. a suffixed literal's ':int32' wins over a bare reserved word.

binder-head.comment: §2.4 binder heads: the region between a binder (λ Λ forall ∀) and the dot that terminates it. At bracket depth zero bare names are SINGLE dot-free segments and the terminating '.' is STRUCTURAL (not part of a qualified name). A dotted name here must be backtick-escaped; inside nested <...>/(...)/backticks dots read greedily as usual. This begin/end scope claims the glyph + head so the greedy #qualified-name rule cannot glue 'y.either' (binder name + terminating dot + following keyword) into one token. The head ends at the first depth-zero '.'; nested '<...>' groups and backticks are consumed as inner patterns so their dots do not end the head.

patterns.comment: A nested type-argument group '<...>' inside a binder-head domain type, where dots read greedily. Recurses into the full expression so inner qualified names, nested groups, etc. tokenize normally; the group's own dots never terminate the head.
A nested parenthesized group inside a binder-head (e.g. a kinded binder '(f : * → *)' RESERVED #226, or a parenthesized domain type). Dots inside read greedily.
The ':' separating a binder name from its domain type (λx:t. / kinded forall).
patterns.name: punctuation.separator.type.hydra

patterns.comment: Separator between multiple binder names (∀x,y.).
patterns.name: punctuation.separator.binder.hydra

patterns.comment: Literal type names appearing as a bare binder-head domain (λx:int32.body).
patterns.name: support.type.hydra

patterns.comment: A single dot-free segment: a binder name OR a bare single-segment domain type name. (Dotted names at depth zero would be a spec violation unless backticked, handled above.)
patterns.name: variable.parameter.hydra

patterns.comment: Doc comment (§6.2): '## ...' or a bare '##' separator line. Structured EntityMetadata, distinct from the whitespace-class '#' line comment. Must precede the plain-comment rule so '##' is not eaten as '#'.
patterns.name: comment.block.documentation.hydra

patterns.comment: @key metadata lines inside a doc comment (§6.2): @seeAlso @availableSince @deprecatedSince @requirement @recommendation.
patterns.name: keyword.other.documentation.directive.hydra

patterns.comment: Plain line comment (§2.2): '#' to end of line. Not special inside strings/backticks (handled by those rules consuming first).
patterns.name: comment.line.number-sign.hydra

module-header.comment: §6.1: 'module' <moduleName>. moduleName is a dotted name read greedily.

import-decl.comment: §6.1/§6.3: 'import' <moduleName> [as <alias>] [from <package>]. Alias and package may be dotted.

definition-keywords.comment: §6.1: definition kinds and their modifiers. 'type'/'term'/'primitive' with optional 'impure'/'partial' prefixes. These are also in the §2.7 reserved list; captured here at line start to additionally mark the defined name.

patterns.comment: A definition line: [impure] [partial] (type|term|primitive) <localName>. localName captured as the defined entity.

strings.comment: §2.5: JSON string syntax and escapes. '#' is NOT special inside a string.
strings.name: string.quoted.double.hydra

patterns.comment: JSON escapes: \" \\ \b \f \n \r \t and \u00xx (lowercase hex per §2.5).
patterns.name: constant.character.escape.hydra

patterns.comment: §2.6 Binary literal: a JSON string immediately followed by ':binary'. Matched before plain strings would be, but since the string body is complex we tag the ':binary' suffix and let the string rule handle the quotes via a separate higher-level include is impractical; here we only tag the suffix that abuts a closing quote.
§2.6 Float literal with mandatory precision suffix, incl. non-finite sentinels: 0.42:float32, 2.5e10:float64, NaN:float64, Infinity:float32, -Infinity:float64.
§2.6 Integer literal with mandatory width suffix: 42:int32, -7:int64.

§2.6 Decimal literal (arbitrary precision): a bare JSON number with NO suffix. Must NOT be followed by ':' + a width/float keyword (those are handled above). Negative lookahead on the suffix avoids double-matching the leading digits of a suffixed literal.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.decimal.hydra

patterns.comment: §2.6 Booleans.
patterns.name: constant.language.boolean.hydra

backtick-name.comment: §2.4: backtick-escaped name `...`, admitting any name (uses the §2.5 string escape set for its content). Example in-use: `_` (escaped reserved word).
backtick-name.name: variable.other.escaped.hydra

keywords-reserved.comment: §2.7 reserved words, reserved in all positions. Split by role for richer highlighting. A reserved word is NOT highlighted as such when backtick-escaped — the #backtick-name rule consumes those first.

patterns.comment: Type-constructor and type-level keywords (§3 types + literal type names).
patterns.name: support.type.hydra

patterns.comment: Term-level keywords: binders, eliminators, constructors, let (§3).
patterns.name: keyword.control.hydra

patterns.comment: The case-default / anonymous wildcard '_' (reserved; backtick form handled separately).
patterns.name: keyword.other.wildcard.hydra

patterns.comment: Float non-finite sentinel bare keywords NaN/Infinity when not part of a suffixed literal (those are handled in #literals).
patterns.name: constant.language.float.hydra

operators-unicode.comment: §2.3 Unicode operators/binders. λ Λ ∀ → ⇒ ⟨ ⟩. 'forall' (the keyword, §2.3) is handled as a type keyword above; ∀ is the type-scheme binder here.

operators-ascii.comment: §2.3 ASCII tokens. ':=' (let bindings) before '=' (fields/map entries) before ':' (ascription). '@' annotation marker.

type-brackets.comment: §3: '<' '>' are type-argument delimiters (list<t>, map<k,v>, either<a,b>, effect<t>, optional<t>, set<t>) — structural punctuation, NOT operators. The #811 comparison operators share the '<'/'>' glyphs but are forward-looking and parse-only; the pervasive landed role is the delimiter, so single '<'/'>' tokenize as brackets here. The unambiguous 2-char comparison tokens ('<=' '>=' '==') are still tagged as reserved comparison operators in #operators-reserved (matched before this rule).

operators-reserved.comment: forward-looking (#811): operator / pipeline sugar that the spec (§3) reserves but the parser does not yet accept. A TextMate grammar only tokenizes, so highlighting these early is harmless. NOTE on '-': per §2.6 '-' occurs only inside numeric literals today; the #literals rules match a numeric '-' first, so a standalone '-' reaching here is only the (reserved) binary-minus operator. '<' and '>' are deliberately EXCLUDED (they are type-argument delimiters, see #type-brackets); only the unambiguous 2-char comparison tokens are here.

nominal-sugar.comment: §3 nominal sugar (#809, LANDED): a type name immediately before '{...}' or '[...]' (NO intervening whitespace) is nominal construction/elimination. We tag the name as a type reference; the braces/brackets fall through to normal punctuation. The abutting (?=[{\[]) lookahead enforces the no-space rule — 'Name {' (with a space) is ordinary application and NOT matched here.
nominal-sugar.name: entity.name.type.nominal.hydra

qualified-name.comment: §2.4: a bare dotted name, read greedily as one qualified name (hydra.core.model.Term). Primitive references and variables share this form (§3 variableTerm). The last segment starting uppercase hints a type/constructor; we keep a single scope for simplicity and let themes distinguish via the dotted punctuation.

patterns.comment: Qualified (dotted) name — at least one dot.
patterns.name: variable.other.qualified.hydra

patterns.comment: Single-segment name (variable, binder name, field name).
patterns.name: variable.other.hydra
